title: The Dat-e Adolescence Prevention Program Protocol: A Cluster Randomized Control Trial
author: Virginia Sanchez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tp8emrw
materials: and materials will be used (available upon request to the Principal Investigator). Students received no rewards or incentives for taking part in the program. Outcomes In order to assess the efficacy of the program, different outcomes will be measured: Behavioural Outcomes: • Physical Aggression and Victimization (MCTS_R, 18): • Psychological Aggression and Victimization (19): • Online Aggression and Victimization (20): Cognitive outcomes: Myths of romantic love (adapted version of Myths of romantic love scale, 21) • omnipotence myth • jealousy myth • better half myth • eternal passion myth Couple context outcomes: • Conflicts (NRI, 22). • Intimacy (Triangular Love Scale, 23). • Online intimacy (CBD Q-A, 24). Emotional outcomes: • Anger regulation (EQ-YV, 25). • Self-esteem (26):

steps.title: Select and Screen Schools
steps.instruction: Identify 15 public or partially funded secondary schools in the South of Spain (Seville and Córdoba) that possess a medium economic, social, and cultural level (ISC Index).

steps.title: Recruit and Inform School Principals
steps.instruction: Engage school leadership to explain the project's aims, contents, and procedures.

substeps.instruction: Send a presentation letter to the Principals of the 15 selected schools.
Conduct personal interviews with Principals at each school.

steps.title: Allocate Schools to Groups
steps.instruction: Assign schools to either the experimental or control group using a coin toss procedure managed by the research team.

substeps.instruction: Implement a waiting list procedure for control group schools interested in future intervention.

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent
steps.instruction: Ensure all necessary legal permissions are secured before student participation.

substeps.instruction: Have school Principals communicate project aims to families, teachers, and the School Board.
Collect completed informed consent forms from families or school boards.

steps.title: Select Participating Students
steps.instruction: Identify the student cohort (approximately 2,000 students, ages 12-16) who will participate in the trial.

substeps.instruction: In schools with more than two classes per grade, have Principals select the specific classes to receive the intervention.
Arrange for students who refuse to participate to attend alternative lessons during school time.

steps.title: Conduct Pre-Test Data Collection
steps.instruction: Administer the first wave of data collection during school time using anonymous pen-and-pencil self-reports.

substeps.instruction: Assign a unique identification code to each student to ensure anonymity and longitudinal tracking.

steps.title: Implement the Prevention Program
steps.instruction: Deliver the Dat-e Adolescence prevention program, implemented by trained researchers using a toolkit manual.

substeps.instruction: Deliver the student curricular-based module consisting of seven lessons (1 hour per week).

steps.title: Conduct Post-Test Data Collection
steps.instruction: Administer the second wave of pen-and-pencil self-reports one week after the intervention is completed.

steps.title: Conduct Follow-Up Data Collection
steps.instruction: Administer the third wave of pen-and-pencil self-reports 6 months after the intervention.

steps.title: Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Process and analyze the collected data using SPSS and M-PLUS software.

substeps.instruction: Code data using trained collaborators following procedures established in seminars by the Principal Investigator.
Code only gender and age for participants; exclude all other personal information.
Test longitudinal measurement invariance for all measures across the three waves.
Apply Latent Change Score and Latent Growth Models to predict longitudinal development and intervention effects.
